title: On-screen ChatGPT usage windows via Little Mester MCP
objective: Add a low-priority, read-only Little Mester MCP module and on-screen counter for authenticated ChatGPT usage in the five-hour and weekly windows, after confirming a supported and safe source for the data.

acceptance_criteria.text: The implementation uses a supported, documented source for the authenticated account's five-hour and weekly usage windows; discovery records whether the source provides token counts, quota percentages, reset times, and plan-specific limits. It never labels another metric as tokens or fabricates unavailable values.

A read-only Little Mester MCP tool reports the available five-hour and weekly usage, remaining quota or percentage, and reset information with explicit units and collection time; it handles unsupported plans, missing data, and source outages clearly.
A compact on-screen counter presents both windows and their reset state, refreshes at a bounded rate, and remains legible without disrupting existing TUI/sidebar content.

Authentication uses the existing supported OpenCode credential boundary; credentials, authorization headers, and raw usage responses containing sensitive account data are not logged, persisted in the workspace, or exposed through unrelated MCP tools.
The module is opt-in or safely unavailable when the required provider/auth is absent, performs no quota-changing actions, and does not broaden host/network exposure or egress policy.

Automated tests cover parsing and units, five-hour/weekly windows and reset boundaries, missing/unsupported responses, authentication failures, refresh behavior, and secret/log redaction; owner verification confirms the displayed values against the supported account UI/source.

needed: Research and document the supported ChatGPT/OpenAI usage endpoint or API available to the authenticated OpenCode account; confirm allowed use, response semantics, and whether the source exposes tokens versus quota percentage/request limits before implementation.

Define the MCP tool response schema and the on-screen TUI placement/refresh policy; coordinate with existing token metrics ticket #24 so session token totals are not confused with provider quota windows.
Add unit and integration tests for five-hour and weekly usage/reset parsing, units, boundaries, unsupported plans, missing fields, provider errors, and redaction.
Owner acceptance: compare both displayed windows and reset times with the provider's supported account usage view; confirm no credentials or sensitive response data are logged or persisted.
